hstad-10026-loc00713-01-rel22-1717-06-16.summary: Chancellor Sinzendorf, by order of Charles VI, proposes to Wackerbarth (and the day before to Saint-Saphorin) a concert of the Emperor, the King of Poland and the King of England to restore the tranquillity of the Empire and an entire peace in the North on a just balance; Saint-Saphorin, as Wackerbarth reports it ('Selon lui'), thinks it might go as far as a triple alliance (his opinion, not Sinzendorf's proposal); the stay of the Russians in the Empire is referred to the Diet of Ratisbon and the directors of the Circles; George I wants the same measures regarding Poland and nothing returned to the King of Sweden; strict secrecy.
hstad-10026-loc00713-01-rel22-1717-06-16.en:
[view 0089] Although I have so far told Your [Majesty] that, to all appearances, the Imperial Court would try to gain time,
which might enlighten it on the outcome of the campaign in Hungary, before it made known its true sentiments regarding the
affairs of the North, I have nevertheless omitted nothing that could enlighten me more closely, having to this end constantly
continued to make suitable representations,

[view 0090] until at last Count [Sinzendorf], Chancellor of the Court, let me know last Monday that he had orders to speak
to me on behalf of the Emperor; that he would come from [Laxenburg] to <306>, and that he asked me to meet him at his house
then.

hstad-10026-loc00713-01-w-f-1717-04-24.summary: The King of Sweden's designs on Poland (a landing near Danzig); the fear that Sweden may detach the Czar from the Northern League, which Vienna should thwart; the Hanau exchange: the Electors' consents must be won directly, not through the Emperor (promise of Ferdinand II to John George I); request for full power and a draft treaty.
hstad-10026-loc00713-01-w-f-1717-04-24.en:
This translates the decipherment of the time, the sheet at ff. 33-33v (views 0042-0043), as we transcribed it in
frozen/releves/A-FEUILLE-0042-0043.txt. That sheet renders the whole cipher of ff. 29-32. Our own decoding with key c
(a24reading.md, 90.8% of 207 cipher words) agrees with it in sense throughout.

[Concerning the] views of the King of Sweden on Poland, this further detail is added: his intention is to attempt a landing
on the side of Danzig; but nothing is said of Stanislas. A person who is, it is true, of no great rank, but who frequents
some houses of the first ministers and has credit there, told me on this occasion that this design of the King of Sweden
could not embarrass us as long as we were sure of the Czar's good intentions.

hstad-10026-loc00712-05-w-wife-1715-11-2.summary: Answering a 'reasoning' put to the countess at the imperial court, Wackerbarth says that Charles XII will be driven from the Empire (Stralsund closely besieged, Wismar blockaded since Poel was taken); Augustus II wants a general peace, not a separate one, and no total ruin of Sweden; the remnants that might carry Charles XII back to Poland should be destroyed now; he will write to General Dücker and ask Count Virmond to come, so that peace may be made under the Emperor's mediation.
hstad-10026-loc00712-05-w-wife-1715-11-2.en:
Wackerbarth to his wife, the Countess of Wackerbarth, in Vienna (copy; see s15reading.md for the attribution). Translation of
s15reading.md (v2), the clear and the cipher words together, as one text. Marks: [x] = restored word; <...> = unresolved
(number given); (...) = our gloss; "…" = clear text not transcribed in full. Probable words are not marked here (see
s15reading.md). Read in part: 80.4% under the target's one strict rule (96.75% by the contributor's count, which counts words resting on values deduced in the letter).

[view 0380, f. 307] (Heading:) Answer to the letter from Vienna. At the camp before Stralsund, 20 November 1715 ("9bre"; first transcribed "8bre", see NOTES.md).
I have seen by yours of the 5th of this month … a line of reasoning that was put to you on the interest of the allies of the
North with regard to the King of Sweden.
